data.title: ICF: Resilient Results and Attractive Valuation Support Buy Despite Price Target Cut to €8.5
data.description:
Industrie Chimiche Forestali SpA, the Basic Materials sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Andrea Zampaloni from Alantra Equities maintained a Buy rating on the stock and has a €8.50 price target.

Andrea Zampaloni has given his Buy rating due to a combination of resilient results and an attractive valuation. ICF’s revenue and EBITDA both increased during the first nine months of 2026, despite a softer third quarter reflecting weak leather and luxury demand and the reversal of a temporary inventory benefit. Continued support from packaging and industrial applications indicates that the business retains useful market diversification.

Cash generation remained healthy, reducing net debt even after shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks, while the balance sheet remains relatively lightly leveraged. The shares trade at modest forward EV/EBITDA multiples and offer compelling dividend and free-cash-flow yields. Although estimates were trimmed and the price target was revised down from €8.8 to €8.5, the analyst still sees substantial upside of approximately 37%, supporting the confirmed Buy recommendation.

data.title: Builders FirstSource: Buy Rating Reaffirmed as Strategic Initiatives Support Upside; $78 Price Target Unchanged
data.description:
In a report released today, Charles Perron-Piche from Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy rating on Builders Firstsource, with a price target of $78.00.

Charles Perron-Piche gave his rating based on several factors, including stronger confidence in Builders FirstSource’s strategic initiatives and the possibility that earnings will reach a cyclical low around 2027. Management outlined a plan to generate roughly $925 million of EBITDA improvement by 2031 through greater customer wallet share, productivity gains, and disciplined acquisitions. Scale, component capabilities, and supplier relationships could support about 200 basis points of annual above-market sales growth, while digital and supply-chain efforts are expected to contribute $300 million in net savings.

Perron-Piche estimates these initiatives could deliver at least an 11% EBITDA compound annual growth rate through 2031, reaching approximately $1.9 billion without a broader market recovery and potentially $2.5 billion if conditions normalize. The company’s balance-sheet flexibility also allows $3.5–$5.5 billion of capital deployment over five years. Although near-term housing demand remains uncertain, he believes much of the risk is reflected in the valuation; with the $78 price target unchanged and implying substantial upside, the risk-reward profile supports a Buy rating.

In another report released today, Barclays also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $70.00 price target.

data.title: Autodesk: Cautious Outlook Amid Weakening Reseller Confidence; Price Target Unchanged at $276
data.description:
Citi analyst Tyler Radke reiterated a Hold rating on Autodesk yesterday and set a price target of $276.00.

Tyler Radke gave his rating based on several factors, including a sharp weakening in reseller confidence ahead of Autodesk’s third-quarter results. Lower quota achievement, negative forward growth expectations, rising macroeconomic concerns, and limited benefits from price increases suggested that demand could soften.

Although Radke expected the company to perform near the top of its quarterly guidance, he anticipated a more cautious fourth-quarter outlook as transaction-related growth benefits fade. The MaintainX acquisition and elevated enterprise agreement activity could support near-term results, but they did not offset uncertainty around organic growth, so the price target remained unchanged at $276.
